findings.what:
NETWORK-FAILURE BRANCH with a duplicate-safe retry. This is needed now: at 15:05-15:35Z api.kaggle.com DNS failed, the E10/feed loops hung and the 15:17Z round cron did not fire. The risk: a submit whose response is lost may still have landed, and a blind retry would then burn one of the 5 slots of 29 Sep, i.e. a morning file.
NETWORK-FAILURE BRANCH (DNS NameResolutionError, 'Max retries exceeded', timeouts, HTTP 5xx or 429). It runs as ONE background script per file (Bash run_in_background, so a sleep inside it is allowed and the session is re-invoked when it exits). A submit is never repeated unless a list call has succeeded and shows the exp token absent.
nb_try() { tok=$1; kid=$2; msg=$3; t0=$(date +%s)
 for w in 0 30 60 120 240 300 300 150; do
  [ $w -gt 0 ] && sleep $w
  L=$(timeout 180 python -m kaggle competitions submissions $C -v 2>&1)
  if ! printf '%s\n' "$L" | grep -q '^ref,'; then echo "$(date -u +%TZ) LIST FAIL $(printf '%s' "$L" | tail -1 | cut -c1-120)"; continue; fi
  printf '%s\n' "$L" | python -c "import sys,csv;sys.path.insert(0,'tools');from runtime_ledger import exp_token;r=list(csv.DictReader(sys.stdin));sys.exit(0 if any(exp_token(x['description']) in sys.argv[1].split(',') for x in r) else 1)" "$tok" && { echo "ALREADY SUBMITTED ($tok)"; return 0; }
  O=$(timeout 300 python -m kaggle competitions submit $C -k $kid -v 1 -f submission.csv -m "$msg" 2>&1); echo "$(date -u +%TZ) $(printf '%s' "$O" | tail -1 | cut -c1-160)"
  printf '%s' "$O" | grep -q 'Successfully submitted' && return 0
  if printf '%s' "$O" | grep -qiE 'limit|not found|forbidden|unauthori|40[0134]' && ! printf '%s' "$O" | grep -qiE 'NameResolution|Max retries|timed out|50[0-9]|429'; then echo "HARD FAIL $tok"; return 2; fi
 done; echo "GAVE UP after $(( ($(date +%s)-t0)/60 )) min"; return 1; }
# usage (tok for the stack = 'exp89r,exp89q', so neither variant can be sent twice):
# nb_try exp89r,exp89q vitaliineibauer/biohub-exp89r-k2cap6-k-sec-dis225-ci "probe 52: exp89r = ..."
EXIT 0 -> continue the batch (G2, then the ledger). EXIT 2 -> hard failure (exp89p -> exp83c fallback; a stack variant -> the other variant only if its dummy PASSED and 51's code allows it (exp89q is always allowed); exp75 -> nothing replaces it; push the user). EXIT 1 (20 min without success) -> PushNotification (load it with ToolSearch 'select:PushNotification'), text:
'Ночная отправка 29.09: Kaggle API недоступен с <HH:MM> МСК (<DNS/HTTP ошибка>). Не отправлены: <probe 52 exp89r/q, probe 53 exp75, probe 54 exp89p>. Сессия повторяет каждые 10 мин. Сроки: файлы с CI до 11:30 МСК, exp89p до 14:30 МСК (правило LATE). Действий не нужно; при желании вручную: <одна команда submit>.'
Then re-run nb_try every 10 min (a session cron or a background loop) until the file's LATE cutoff. Files that wait for a free slot go in list order. Also, if the network outage also hung the E10 watch or feed loop (as at 15:05-15:35Z), kill and restart them once the network is back (as at 15:41Z). The poller survives by itself (timeout 180).
